    Global facts about the ray category of a minimal representation-infinite algebra #

    Two consequences of minimality used in [mild] §4, stated for a ray category:

    • NoProjInj: no nonzero μ₀ : x ⟶ z is both the unique right-deep ray out of x and the unique left-deep ray into z (no projective-injective B e_x);
    • NoSplit: no point z splits the category into a receiver part and an emitter part with nonzero morphisms on both sides.

    Both are symmetric under passing to Pᵒᵖ (NoProjInj.op, NoSplit.op).

    Prop

    μ is killed by every non-invertible morphism after it.

            def LargeIndecomposable.RayCat.TinyAt {Q : Type u_1} [CategoryTheory.Category.{u_2, u_1} Q] [CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroMorphisms Q] {x z b : Q} (s : x ⟶ z) (t : x ⟶ b) :
            Prop

            A tiny penny-farthing point x ([Standard] §3.1, §3.2): s : x ⟶ z is the unique left-deep ray into z, the right-deep rays out of x are s and an irreducible t : x ⟶ b (b ≠ z, b ≠ x), and every non-invertible morphism into b factors through t. Then the indecomposables not killed by s are B e_x and B e_x / (t) (RepresentationType/MinimalInfinite/Tiny.lean), so B is not minimal representation-infinite.
